title: Constructible sheaves over a discrete Noetherian ring form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], regarded as discrete. On the small étale or small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call a sheaf constructible if, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, there is a finite partition $U=\coprod_{a<n} Z_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], [def-weil-constructible-subset], with immersion maps $Z_a\to U$, such that the inverse-image restriction to each $Z_a$ (the module inverse image along $Z_a\to U\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]) is locally constant with finitely presented $R$-module values: locally on the site of $Z_a$, as module sheaves on the localized sites, it is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely presented $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf], [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. On either site the constructible sheaves contain zero and are closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between constructible sheaves, and under extensions: if $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ is exact and $F,G$ are constructible, then $E$ is constructible. In other words they form a weak Serre subcategory, with the displayed closure properties as its meaning. No finiteness of the underlying set of $R$ and no invertibility on $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: Étale part, implemented: identify finite generated constant local models with the existing IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf predicate. A geometric point lifts through an étale cover, and its stalk is the displayed constant module. Conversely discard empty cover members and evaluate at a separably closed residue-field point; its finitely generated stalk makes the constant value finitely generated. No finiteness of R as a set is used. Apply this equivalence to each affine-local stratum.

Étale part, implemented: use Stratification.inter on the two partitions of each affine open. Its strata are actual fibre products. Apply finite local constancy under upperStar to the two projections and upperStarComp to identify these iterated restrictions with restriction to the common stratum.

Étale part, implemented: restriction upperStar is exact. Apply the existing Noetherian kernel and cokernel lemmas for finite locally constant module-valued sheaves on each common stratum and transport across PreservesKernel.iso and PreservesCokernel.iso.

Étale part, implemented: prove extension closure over an arbitrary Noetherian coefficient ring by generalizing the existing lifted-presentation proof. Present the constant quotient N by R^b with b finite. Locally lift its finitely many basis images. The relation module ker(p) is finitely generated by Noetherianity; choose a finite generating set t and refine until the images of just these generators in the constant submodule are constant. The linear combination of lifted sections has range contained in the constant submodule, since this holds on the chosen generators. Invert the injection of that submodule on its range to obtain the relation map ker(p) to M. The existing isConstant_over_of_shortExact_of_lift identifies the middle sheaf with the constant pushout. Compose the covers; exactness on stalks gives finite generation of the middle stalks. This supplies noetherian_flc_of_shortExact without assuming Finite R.

proof.text: Étale part, implemented: the trivial stratification and the zero constant module show zero constructible. The scalar restriction functor etaleConstantModuleRestrictionFunctor is an equivalence, using its existing unit and counit. It therefore preserves kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. Transport the module-valued affine-local closure proved above through this equivalence. The resulting public theorem has only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound in its axiom list.

Pro-etale part, implemented: the local-model predicate is exactly the local clause of the existing affine constructibility definition. The zero module is finitely presented. On every localized site its constant module sheaf is zero because module sheafification preserves zero. Inverse image is additive and preserves zero, so the trivial one-stratum partition of each affine open witnesses zero constructible, including the empty scheme.

Pro-etale part, implemented: on each affine open intersect the finite stratifications of the two given constructible sheaves using Stratification.inter. For each projection from a common stratum, the proved local-model pullback lemma preserves its finitely presented local values. The canonical module pullback composition isomorphism identifies this iterated inverse image with restriction along the composite immersion to X. Thus both sheaves have finitely presented constant local models on every common stratum.

Pro-etale part, implemented: apply exact canonical constant-coefficient module inverse image to a map or short exact sequence on each common stratum. The proved local-model weak Serre theorem supplies finite-presentation local models for the kernel and cokernel, or middle term. Transport along PreservesKernel.iso and PreservesCokernel.iso in the first two cases. The common stratification has constructible strata and therefore witnesses the required affine-local constructibility. The three resulting clauses are precisely the public pro-etale theorem.

tool_uses.why: Converts finite type to finitely presented values over the given Noetherian ring; this is a generic commutative algebra tool, with no replacement in the integral-model unit.
Supplies the étale geometric inverse image and its algebraic-structure compatibility, used only to restrict to strata.
Generic geometric-morphism tool giving colimit and finite-limit preservation for constant coefficients and trivializing covers.
Generic site inverse-image exactness, used to restrict the exact sequence; no integral-model assertion replaces it.
Generic common-refinement tool for the two finite constructibility witnesses.
Generic adjunction-compatible composition of inverse images, identifying restriction through either old stratum with restriction to the common stratum.
Generic weak-Serre theorem on any small site for an arbitrary Noetherian coefficient ring, used separately on each stratum; the integral-model unit has no local substitute.
Generic base-change stability of arbitrary étale covering families, used to pull the original trivializing covers to the common strata.

Generic commutation of inverse image with localization (Stacks 04J0), identifying restrictions of pulled-back sheaves to members of the pulled-back trivializing covers; the integral-model unit has no local substitute.
